patients.summary: Graduate student with generalized epilepsy, seizure-free for years on levetiracetam, who joined the practice in 2023. In 2025 a planned switch to lamotrigine ended in a drug eruption and a permanent lamotrigine allergy, and that fall she had a breakthrough tonic-clonic seizure treated in an outside ED, after which neurology raised her levetiracetam.

documents.title: New patient intake call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is starting a grad program at the university this fall and moved to town last week. Wants a primary care doctor here instead of going back home for care. Has epilepsy, sees a neurology group already and plans to keep seeing them. Student health plan card info taken, verified active. Booked new patient physical 9/12 at 8:40. Mailed records release for her old primary care office and emailed the intake packet. Reminded her to bring her med bottle.

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
24F, new to the practice, first-year grad student. Here to set up primary care locally.

Epilepsy: first convulsive seizures at 16, worked up and diagnosed by a pediatric neurologist, on levetiracetam since. Last seizure she can recall was around age 19. Takes levetiracetam 500 mg twice a day, rarely misses, keeps it in a pill case. Neuro follows her once a year (outside group) and writes the prescription; she intends to stay with them. No side effects she can name.

PMH: as above. PSH: tonsils out at age 8. No other hospital stays.
Meds: levetiracetam 500 mg BID.
Allergies: none known.
FH: father with hypertension, mother with hypothyroidism, a cousin on her mother's side has epilepsy.
SH: graduate student, lives with a roommate. Never smoked. Alcohol maybe once a month or less, a single drink. No other substances.

ROS negative across the board.

Exam: well-appearing. Vitals as charted, BMI about 22. HEENT clear, TMs normal, no thyroid enlargement. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin without rash. Neuro: CN intact, strength and reflexes symmetric, gait normal.

A/P:
1. Epilepsy, well controlled on levetiracetam. Continue; neurology manages. Will request their last note.
2. Health maintenance: CBC, CMP (on an antiseizure med), lipids once, HIV and hep C screening today; she agrees. Records release signed for old PCP office for immunizations and Pap history. Flu and COVID vaccines at a nurse visit next month once the fall supply is in.
3. PHQ-2 is 0.
Next physical in about a year.

documents.title: Your recent lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Emily, all of your blood work from Tuesday came back normal: blood counts and kidney and liver tests are normal, your cholesterol is fine for your age, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens are negative. Nothing to do on your end. Good meeting you.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Records received from prior primary care office (14 pages), abstracted by MA:
- Immunizations: HPV two-dose series 2011 and 2012; Tdap 6/2021; COVID mRNA primary series spring 2021. Childhood series complete per their record.
- Cervical cytology 2021: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.
- Problem list there: epilepsy, on levetiracetam per neurology.
- No allergies recorded.
Immunizations entered. Scanned to media tab for PCP review.

documents.title: Immunization visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for fall vaccines. Screening questions negative, no prior vaccine reactions. Influenza 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. Updated COVID mRNA IM right deltoid. Lot numbers and VIS dates in the immunization record. Observed 15 minutes, no issues, left ambulatory.

documents.title: Neurology annual follow-up letter
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Outpatient Neurology — annual epilepsy visit, seen 01/16/2024

Dear colleague,

I saw Ms. Ouellette for her yearly epilepsy review. She has generalized epilepsy with tonic-clonic seizures beginning in adolescence and has had no events in roughly five years on levetiracetam monotherapy. She reports good adherence and no mood or sleep complaints she attributes to the drug. Her move for graduate school has gone smoothly.

Examination today was normal, including mental status, cranial nerves, motor, sensory, coordination and gait.

Impression: generalized epilepsy, in remission on levetiracetam.

Plan: continue levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily; 90-day prescription sent with refills. Seizure precautions reviewed. I will see her in one year, sooner for any event.

Allergies: none known.
Medications: levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily.

With thanks for allowing me to share in her care,
Attending neurologist

documents.title: Keppra refill
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, my pharmacy says my last refill on the levetiracetam ran out and they're waiting on the neurology office, which hasn't answered in two days. I have about 4 days of pills left. Is there any way you could send a short supply so I don't run out? Sorry for the bother.

documents.title: RE: Keppra refill
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: No bother at all. I sent a 30-day supply of levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily to your usual pharmacy, same dose as always. Please keep nudging the neurology office for the long-term prescription. Don't skip doses while you wait.

documents.title: RE: Immunization record
documents.author: MA

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam. Second year of her program, busy but doing well.

Epilepsy: no seizures. Levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily, the neurology office sorted out the refill problem in the spring. Saw neuro in January, no changes. Sleeping 7 hours most nights.

Meds: levetiracetam 500 mg BID. Allergies: NKDA.
SH unchanged; never smoker, alcohol rare.
PHQ-9 = 2.

Exam: vitals as charted. Pleasant, well. Neck supple, no nodes or thyroid enlargement. Cardiac regular rhythm, no murmurs. Lungs clear throughout. Abd soft, no masses. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, vaginal walls normal, cervix without lesions; cytology collected. Skin clear. Neuro grossly intact.

A/P:
- Epilepsy in remission on levetiracetam; continue, neuro follows.
- Pap due (last 2021): collected today, cytology alone at her age.
- CBC and CMP for medication monitoring.
- Flu and updated COVID given today.
Return in a year.

documents.title: Pap and labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Emily, your Pap test was normal, and your blood counts and chemistry panel look fine too. The next Pap would be due in three years. Have a good semester.

documents.title: Neurology follow-up letter
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Outpatient Neurology — epilepsy follow-up, seen 04/14/2025

Dear colleague,

Ms. Ouellette returns for her yearly visit. She remains free of seizures on levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily. She asked about alternatives for long-term treatment, and after going over the options together we agreed on a gradual transition to lamotrigine.

Neurological examination is normal.

Plan:
1. Start lamotrigine 25 mg daily for two weeks, then 50 mg daily. We will reassess before any further increase.
2. Continue levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily unchanged until lamotrigine is at target; a taper schedule will follow.
3. I reviewed the risk of a serious rash with lamotrigine. She knows to stop the medication and call us the same day for any new rash, fever, mouth sores or swollen glands.

Allergies: none known.
Medications: levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily; lamotrigine as above.

Attending neurologist

documents.title: Rash
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Since yesterday I have an itchy red rash on my stomach and back and this morning it's on my arms and legs too. I started lamotrigine about three weeks ago and went up to 2 pills last week. No fever, my mouth and eyes are fine. Neurology told me to call about any rash. Should I come in to you or them?

documents.title: RE: Rash
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for messaging right away. Please call the neurology office as soon as they open and tell them you have a rash on lamotrigine; they will want to see you quickly and decide about the medicine. Keep taking your levetiracetam as usual. If you get a fever, blisters, sores in your mouth or eyes, or feel unwell, go to the emergency department instead. Let me know what they say.

documents.title: RE: Rash
documents.author: patient
documents.body: They're seeing me tomorrow morning. Thank you.

documents.title: Neurology urgent visit letter
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Outpatient Neurology — urgent visit, seen 05/06/2025

Dear colleague,

I saw Ms. Ouellette at short notice for a rash. She began lamotrigine on 04/14 as part of a planned switch from levetiracetam and moved to 50 mg daily about a week ago. Two days before this visit she noticed itching and redness over the trunk, which has since extended to both arms and legs. She has had no fever, no involvement of the mouth, eyes or genitals, and she feels otherwise well.

Medications: levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily; lamotrigine 50 mg daily (stopped today).

Examination: vital signs normal. Scattered erythematous macules and papules over the trunk and all four limbs. No blisters, bullae, skin sloughing or targetoid lesions. Mucous membranes clear. No enlarged lymph nodes.

Labs today: complete blood count, comprehensive metabolic panel with liver tests, and creatinine all normal.

Impression: maculopapular drug eruption due to lamotrigine. There is no fever, mucosal disease or organ involvement at present, so this does not meet criteria for DRESS or SJS, but given that risk with this drug I have stopped lamotrigine permanently.

Plan:
1. Lamotrigine discontinued today; she should never be rechallenged. Please add lamotrigine to her allergy list (severe cutaneous reaction/DRESS risk).
2. Continue levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily, which she never stopped; she remains protected.
3. She will contact us urgently for fever, blistering, mouth sores or facial swelling.
4. Return in six months, sooner as needed.

Allergies: lamotrigine (drug eruption; do not rechallenge).

Attending neurologist

documents.title: Med list update
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Neurology letter from 5/6 reviewed with PCP. Called pt to confirm: she stopped lamotrigine Tuesday on neuro's instructions and is still taking levetiracetam 500 mg BID, no missed doses. Rash about the same, still itchy, no fever, mouth fine. Lamotrigine removed from active meds and added to allergies, high criticality. Pt aware to message if anything changes.

documents.title: Rash update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just an update — the rash is almost all gone. A little pink on my back still but it doesn't itch anymore. Never got a fever.

documents.title: RE: Rash update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad to hear it. That's the expected course once the medicine is stopped. We have lamotrigine on your allergy list now, so it will flag if anyone tries to prescribe it again.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly visit, 26 now.

Interval: lamotrigine trial in the spring stopped after a maculopapular rash (neuro letter 5/8). Rash cleared within about two weeks, no fever, nothing on the mucosa. Never off levetiracetam, still 500 mg twice a day, no seizures. Neuro plans a recheck in the fall.

Meds: levetiracetam 500 mg BID.
Allergies: LAMOTRIGINE — drug eruption, do not rechallenge (SCAR/DRESS risk).
SH: third year of the program, never smoker, alcohol rarely.
PHQ-9 1.

Exam: vitals as charted, weight stable. NAD. Oropharynx clear, tonsils surgically absent. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen benign. Skin: no residual rash, no hyperpigmentation, no lesions of concern. Neuro intact.

A/P:
- Epilepsy: stable, continue levetiracetam; neuro follow-up as scheduled.
- Lamotrigine eruption: resolved; allergy stays on the list.
- Monitoring labs: CBC, CMP drawn.
- Pap normal 2024, next 2027.
- Flu and COVID vaccines today, both arms, tolerated.
RTC 1 year.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your blood work from the physical is all normal, including the liver and kidney tests. Nothing to change.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Emergency Department Physician Record — date of service 10/24/2025

Arrival: brought in by roommate, private car.

HPI: 26-year-old woman with known epilepsy on levetiracetam. Per her roommate, who witnessed it, she dropped to the floor without warning and was unresponsive, with rhythmic jerking of all four limbs lasting roughly two minutes, followed by a period of unresponsiveness. She came around after about five minutes but was confused and sleepy for a while afterward. She had a drug rash on lamotrigine in May, which was stopped. She takes levetiracetam for seizure control.

PMH: epilepsy. PSH: tonsillectomy at 8.
Medications: levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily.
Allergies: lamotrigine (rash; risk of severe cutaneous reaction).
FH: cousin on mother's side with epilepsy; father hypertension; mother hypothyroidism.
SH: graduate student. Never smoker; alcohol less than once a month.

Vitals on arrival: T 37.2 C (99.0 F), BP 125/78, HR 88, RR 16.

Exam: drowsy, oriented to person, place and time. Lateral tongue bite. Contusion over the left cheek. Neck supple. Heart and lungs unremarkable. Neurologic examination without focal deficit.

Results: Na 138, K 4.2, Cl 100, HCO3 24, BUN 14, Cr 0.9, glucose 98, Ca 9.2. CBC within normal limits. Levetiracetam level sent.

ED course: observed; she returned to her baseline mental status over several hours with no further events.

Impression: breakthrough generalized tonic-clonic seizure in a patient with epilepsy.

Disposition: discharged home with roommate at 02:10. Seizure precautions given. Follow up with her neurologist and primary care physician this week. No driving until cleared.

documents.title: Seizure last night
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I had a seizure last night, my first in years. My roommate took me to the ER and they sent me home around 2am. I feel wiped out and my face is bruised where I hit the floor. They said to follow up with you and neurology. I already left a message for neurology.

documents.title: RE: Seizure last night
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: I'm sorry, that's a scary thing to go through. Rest today and keep taking your levetiracetam exactly as prescribed. Please don't drive, bathe alone, or swim for now. We've put you on the schedule Tuesday afternoon to check in. If you have another seizure, one lasting more than five minutes, or you don't wake up normally afterward, call 911.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Post-ED Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Seen in an outside ED Friday night after a witnessed generalized convulsion, first in about seven years. ED record received yesterday: BMP and CBC normal; levetiracetam level was sent, result not on the copy we received. Discharged the same night. Since then no further events, tired over the weekend and now back to normal. Tongue sore for a couple of days, better. Says she has been taking levetiracetam 500 mg twice a day. Neurology has her booked for 11/12.

Meds: levetiracetam 500 mg BID. Allergies: lamotrigine.

O: Vitals as charted. Alert, conversant, fully oriented. Fading yellow-green bruise over the left cheekbone, nontender, no step-off. Healing bite mark on the side of the tongue. Heart regular, lungs clear. Neuro: CN II–XII intact, strength 5/5 throughout, reflexes symmetric, finger-nose and gait normal.

A/P: Breakthrough generalized tonic-clonic seizure in known epilepsy, back to baseline.
- Continue levetiracetam; any dose change will come from neurology at the 11/12 visit.
- Driving: state rule is six months seizure-free before driving; she does not drive often and understands.
- Seizure safety reviewed: showers rather than baths, no swimming alone, no heights.
- Return in about two months, or sooner if anything happens.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily

documents.title: Neurology follow-up letter
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Outpatient Neurology — follow-up, seen 11/12/2025

Dear colleague,

Ms. Ouellette had a generalized tonic-clonic seizure on 10/24, her first in many years, and was evaluated in an emergency department and discharged. She has had no further events. She remains on levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily and reports no missed doses.

Examination today is normal.

Impression: generalized epilepsy with a single breakthrough seizure.

Plan:
1. Increase levetiracetam to 750 mg twice daily; new prescription sent.
2. Lamotrigine remains contraindicated given her prior eruption.
3. No driving for six months from the date of the seizure.
4. Follow-up in six months.

Allergies: lamotrigine.

Attending neurologist

documents.title: Levetiracetam dose change
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Neuro letter received. Levetiracetam changed to 750 mg BID. Called pt, confirms she picked up the new tablets yesterday and is taking one twice daily; set the old 500 mg bottle aside. Med list updated. Keeping 12/24 appt.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Two-month check after the October seizure. Neurology raised levetiracetam to 750 mg twice daily on 11/12. No seizures, auras or odd spells since. Tolerating the higher dose. Mood fine, PHQ-9 2. Semester wrapped up, heading home for the break this afternoon. Not driving; a friend is taking her.

Meds: levetiracetam 750 mg BID. Allergies: lamotrigine (eruption; do not rechallenge).

Exam: vitals as charted. Well. Cheek bruise gone. Heart RRR, lungs clear. Neuro nonfocal.

A/P:
- Epilepsy, single breakthrough seizure in October, none since on the higher dose. Removing the seizure episode from the active list; epilepsy remains. Neurology follows, next visit in the spring.
- Annual physical due next fall.
Happy holidays.

documents.title: Refill request routed
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy faxed a refill request for levetiracetam 750 mg BID to us. Prescriber of record is her neurologist; called the pharmacy and redirected. They confirm neurology's prescription has 3 refills on file and they will fill from that. No action needed here.

documents.title: Labs before neurology?
documents.author: patient
documents.body: My neurology appointment is in May. Do I need any blood work before it, or should I just wait for my physical in the fall?

documents.title: RE: Labs before neurology?
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Nothing needed from our side before May. If neurology wants a level or other tests they'll order them. We'll do your usual yearly labs at the physical.

documents.title: Neurology follow-up letter
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Outpatient Neurology — follow-up, seen 05/12/2026

Dear colleague,

Ms. Ouellette has had no seizures since 10/24/2025 on levetiracetam 750 mg twice daily, which she tolerates well. Examination is normal.

Impression: generalized epilepsy, controlled.

Plan: continue levetiracetam 750 mg twice daily. She has reached six months seizure-free and may resume driving under state rules. Lamotrigine remains on her allergy list. Return in one year.

Attending neurologist
